title: PO automation, 3-way match, and billing handshake playbook
author: Maya Patel
body:
Overview

This document defines Redwood Inference's standard operating procedure for automating purchase order (PO) creation, executing a three-way match (PO, goods/services receipt, supplier invoice), and ensuring a robust billing handshake with the accounting system (NetSuite). The goal is to reduce manual touchpoints, lower invoice cycle time, and ensure consistent revenue/expense recognition inputs for Finance.

Scope

- Applies to all supplier purchases using a PO that are processed through the procurement system (Coupa) or via approved procurement APIs.
- Excludes petty cash and corporate card transactions (see company card policy).
- Applies to Redwood-hosted deployments for which finance receives invoice data; Private/Enterprise customer billings follow separate product billing procedures.

Goals and success metrics

- Reduce three-way match exception rate to < 3% within 90 days of automation adoption.
- Achieve 95% automated PO-to-invoice matching (no manual intervention).
- Decrease median days-to-payable-confirmation from receipt to AP approval to < 2 days.
- Maintain audit trail with immutable event logs for PO lifecycle (retention 7 years).

Owners and responsibilities

- Procurement (owner): creates PO templates, supplier onboarding, Coupa configuration.
- Accounts Payable (AP) / Finance (owner): final approval gates, GL mapping, NetSuite posting.
- Engineering (platform): maintains integration connectors, webhooks, retry logic, and monitoring dashboards.
- Supplier Success: manages exception communication with vendors.

Primary systems and integrations

- Coupa: PO creation and supplier catalog.
- ERP: NetSuite for AP ledger posting and payments.
- Integration Layer: Redwood Integration Service (RIS) — handles event transformations, idempotency, retries.
- Document Store: S3 CVR bucket for storing supplier PDFs and receipts.
- Observability: Datadog for metrics, Sentry for errors, Kibana for logs.

High-level process flow

1. PO creation
   - Procurement creates a PO in Coupa (or via procurement API). PO fields required: PO number, supplier ID, currency, GL code, cost center, line-item descriptions, quantity, unit price, expected delivery date, tax treatment.
   - Coupa emits po.created event to RIS. RIS validates schema and enriches with internal routing tags (product_area, owner_team, approver_chain).

2. Goods/services receipt (GR)
   - Receiving team confirms delivery in Coupa (or uploads a receipt document). If GR confirmation is not required for a PO type (services subscriptions), a receipt placeholder event is generated automatically after configured acceptance window (default: 7 days).

3. Invoice submission
   - Supplier submits invoice via Coupa supplier portal, EDI, or email-to-invoice ingestion. Invoice must reference PO number. Invoices are stored in S3 and a coupa.invoice.received event is emitted.

4. Three-way match logic (automated)
   - RIS attempts automated matching: match(invoice.po_number, po.lines, gr.receipts, tolerances).
   - Default matching tolerances: line quantity +/- 5%, unit price difference <= 2%, tax and shipping separately matched.
   - If invoice matches within tolerances, RIS forwards to NetSuite with match_status: matched_auto. If outside tolerances or missing PO/GR, match_status: exception and routed to AP inbox.

5. AP review and resolution
   - AP portal shows exceptions with structured fields: reason codes (quantity_mismatch, price_mismatch, missing_receipt, duplicate_invoice, tax_issue).
   - AP performs one of: approve & post, return-to-supplier, request-credit-memo, or escalate to Procurement for PO amendment.

6. Billing handshake with NetSuite (posting)
   - For matched_auto: RIS sends a NetSuite posting payload: {po_number, invoice_id, vendor_id, amount, currency, gl_account, cost_center, attachment_url}.
   - NetSuite responds with posting_id and status. RIS reconciles response and emits invoice.posted event.
   - For exception cases, posting is delayed until AP approves.

Configuration tables (examples)

- PO type configuration
| PO Type | Requires GR | Auto-match tolerance | Post-to-ERP on match? | Default approvers |
|---------|-------------|----------------------|------------------------|-------------------|
| Standard goods | Yes | qty 5%, price 2% | Yes | Department manager + Procurement |
| Services subscription | No (auto-receipt after 7d) | price 0% | Yes | Procurement lead |
| Small spend (<= $2,500) | Optional | price 0% | Yes | Finance delegated approver |

- Exception routing matrix
| Exception code | Primary owner | SLA to resolve | Escalation path |
|----------------|---------------|------------------|------------------|
| missing_receipt | Requester / Receiving | 48 hours | Procurement -> Finance |
| price_mismatch | Procurement | 3 business days | Procurement Ops Manager |
| duplicate_invoice | AP | 24 hours | Vendor -> AP Audit |

JSON examples (events)

- Coupa PO created (emitted to RIS)
{
  "event_type": "po.created",
  "po_number": "PO-2026-0158",
  "supplier_id": "SUP-4420",
  "lines": [ { "line_id": "L1", "qty": 10, "unit_price": 120.00 } ],
  "currency": "USD",
  "requested_by": "eng-team@example.com"
}

- Invoice posted payload to NetSuite
{
  "invoice_id": "INV-9876",
  "po_number": "PO-2026-0158",
  "vendor_id": "SUP-4420",
  "amount": 1200.00,
  "gl_account": "6000-Travel",
  "attachments": ["s3://cvr-bucket/invoices/INV-9876.pdf"]
}

Idempotency and retries

- All RIS outbound messages include an idempotency_key: sha256(invoice_id + event_timestamp). RIS will deduplicate identical keys for 24 hours.
- Retry policy: exponential backoff 5s, 30s, 2m, 10m, 1h; after 5 failures marked for Ops manual review.

Monitoring and KPIs

- Metrics (Datadog): po.created.count, invoice.received.count, match.automatic.rate, match.exception.rate, invoice.time_to_post.median, ap.resolve_time.p95.
- Dashboards: "Procurement Ops" (real-time), "AP Exceptions" (errors and owner lists).
- Alerts: match.exception.rate > 10% sustained for 12 hours -> PagerDuty to Procurement lead. invoice.post.failure.rate > 2% -> Ops alert.

Security and controls

- Access to PO modification requires RBAC: procurement-admin, procurement-editor, read-only.
- All attachments stored in S3 use server-side encryption (AES-256) and access is limited via presigned URLs with 24h TTL.
- Sensitive invoice fields (tax identifiers) masked in logs.

Operational runbook (common incidents)

1. Event: NetSuite posting fails with 5xx
   - Immediate action: RIS retries automatically per retry policy.
   - If retries exhausted: create AP incident, mark affected invoices with posting_failed and notify Finance slack channel #ap-ops.
   - Owner: Integration SRE (primary), AP (secondary).

2. Event: High exception spike (>10%)
   - Triage: Procurement and AP review top 10 exception reasons via dashboard.
   - Quick mitigation: loosen match tolerance for non-financial impact POs or create temporary approval queue.
   - Long-term: identify systemic supplier or catalog issue; schedule supplier outreach.

3. Event: Duplicate invoice suspected
   - Check idempotency_key and s3 attachments. If duplicate detected, mark second invoice as duplicate_invoice and reject with clear reason.

Checklist for new supplier onboarding (procurement + AP)

- Supplier master record created in Coupa with vendor ID.
- Tax forms collected and stored.
- Default GL mapping and cost center templates assigned.
- Supplier invoice method selected (portal/EDI/email) and test invoice sent.
- 72-hour verification window for first invoice to ensure correct matching.

Change control and rollout plan

- Phase 1 (Pilot, 4 weeks): 3 non-critical suppliers, manual review fallback, monitor match rate and incidents.
- Phase 2 (Expand, 8 weeks): 25 suppliers across categories, tune tolerance and enrich POs with additional metadata.
- Phase 3 (Full rollout): All eligible spend categories automated.

- Rollout COB checklist: backup current Coupa-to-NetSuite integration, enable feature flags, ensure AP oncall coverage for first 72 hours, and run daily reconciliation jobs.

Audit and compliance

- Retention: event logs, PO PDFs, and invoice images retained for 7 years per finance policy.
- Audit reports: monthly match-rate report and exception-closure report.
- Internal audit will review a sample (n=50) of auto-matched invoices quarterly.

Appendix: common tolerance guidance

- Services: price must match exactly unless pre-approved amendment.
- Goods: quantity tolerances apply for consumables; capital equipment requires exact match and manual approval.
- Shipping/taxes: matched separately; if tax calculations differ, route to AP tax specialist.
